SPEC GAP in 4.1, measured on the prototype. Adding apple_siwa_tokens to KNOWN_USER_TABLES (E1) also reddens tests/test_migration_043_delete_user_cascade.py::test_precheck_carries_the_c1_c2_c9_sections. That test iterates KNOWN_USER_TABLES over the historical 043 PRECHECK one-paste file and fails with 'PRECHECK never names public.apple_siwa_tokens' ([pyt] tag=b3b-proto-pins). Prototype fix: the precheck test uses KNOWN_USER_TABLES - {'apple_siwa_tokens'}. After it, 043 is 51/51 and the pin set matches base (comm -13 empty). This is a fifth deliberate pin change (E5) that the spec does not list.

Harness hazard found on the prototype. Once APPLE_SIWA_PRIVATE_KEY is in CREDENTIALS_UNSET, the conftest dotenv guard strips it again whenever an import-time load_dotenv(override=True) runs (app.main, extraction_service, url_extraction_service). A row that sets the key before the first app.main import therefore loses it: R6 went red with '[SIWA] config missing: APPLE_SIWA_PRIVATE_KEY'. The RED file's autouse fixture now imports app.main first. Base was re-run after this edit: identical 74/36 and identical reasons.

The spec's 'RED: ModuleNotFoundError' rows (R1-R5 and the others that need the module) are turned into AssertionErrors by a find_spec helper, _siwa(). The standing ruling requires every RED row to fail on an AssertionError.

B3 seam name. Ruling B3 gives only the 6.0 value. The RED file uses the review's name _CALL_DEADLINE: R5 asserts _CALL_DEADLINE == 6.0 and _HTTP_TIMEOUT == 5.0, and R27/R27b patch it to 0.2 s. R27 is split into two nodes: the direct exchange plus revoke (two attempts, each 'failed: TimeoutError'), and the route half (200 with the flag-OFF body).

R9 garbage-key pins the spec 2.9 text '[SIWA] client secret build failed: ValueError'. A non-base64 key raises binascii.Error, whose type name is 'Error', so the implementation must normalise it to ValueError. The prototype does this.
R13 also requires the INFO '[SIWA] no stored token; revoke skipped' for a row whose refresh_token is '' or None (review param), not only when no row is returned.

M4 accepts 'GRANT ... ON public.apple_siwa_tokens' with or without the TABLE keyword, because ruling B6 and the review word it differently. It requires exactly one GRANT, privileges exactly {select, insert, update}, grantee exactly service_role.

Additions beyond the spec rows: an R1 param 'enabled' (False, for X3); an R14 assertion that auth_delete comes after the last revoke; R24 also checks that neutralize_credentials strips the key from a dict environment; R2 accepts any config shape (dict, tuple, dataclass or namespace) holding the four stripped values; R18 checks the user id and email in [SIWA] records only, and the code, tokens, client secrets, PEM body lines, both id_tokens and Apple's error body in every app.* record.
